subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Mild Hybrid Systems
description: A fast breakdown of Mild Hybrid Systems for builders.

hook.text: A mild hybrid adds a small electric motor and 48-volt battery to a regular combustion engine.

buildup.text: The motor can't drive the car alone, but it assists during acceleration and restarts smoothly.

discovery.text: Regenerative braking captures energy that normally becomes brake heat and stores it in the battery.

twist.text: Mild hybrids improve efficiency by about 10 percent—less than a full hybrid but far cheaper.

climax.text: Nearly every European luxury brand now uses 48-volt mild hybrid systems as standard.

punchline.text: A small jolt of electricity makes the combustion engine behave better.

quiz.question: Can a mild hybrid's electric motor drive the car alone?
options: No, it only assists the engine

details.summary: Mild hybrid systems add a small electric motor-generator and a 48-volt battery to a conventional engine, providing electric boost during acceleration, regenerative braking energy, and smoother automatic stop-start.
details.whyItMatters: Mild hybrids improve fuel economy by 10 to 15 percent at relatively low cost and complexity, making them a practical stepping stone for automakers that need to meet emissions targets without going fully electric.
takeaways: A 48-volt system adds electric assist without replacing the engine
Regenerative braking captures energy normally lost as heat
Fuel savings of 10 to 15 percent are typical over conventional engines

faq.question: Can a mild hybrid drive on electricity alone?
faq.answer: No. The electric motor is too small to propel the car independently. It assists the engine during acceleration and powers accessories during coasting and stop-start, but the combustion engine must always be running for propulsion.

faq.question: Why are automakers choosing mild hybrids over full hybrids?
faq.answer: Mild hybrids cost about $1,000 to add to an existing engine, far less than a full hybrid system. They provide enough improvement to help meet emissions targets while keeping vehicle prices competitive.
